executive_assessment.text: Mafraq's Dahiyyat Al-Malik Abdullah study adds local water-network, zoning and displacement-status access barriers, alongside household coping. The small sample and primary role of over-abstraction limit generalization.

The 2023 roadmap describes conditional water/livelihood–cohesion risks; conflict-related displacement and historical water-service pressure are distinct from claims that refugees cause violence. ICRC's evaluation records gains and later operational deterioration.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2026 reports: In Dahiyyat Al-Malik Abdullah, 2022 Amman–Zarqa abstraction was 162.4 MCM versus 87.5 MCM safe yield; the report identifies chronic hydrological drought.
Source dated 2026 reports: Surveyed households: 27% lacked network connection; summer supply fell and 63% reported inadequate pressure.

Source dated 2026 reports: 71% of Syrian versus 25% of Jordanian households had never applied; barriers included zones, fees and landlord support, while Syrians could not register meters individually.
Source dated 2026 reports: Unregulated areas cover 62% of the neighborhood; rural zoning prevents Yarmouk Water Company extending services to some households.
Source dated 2026 reports: GMM's climate-resilient master plan and Urban Observatory support planning; initiatives focus on flood mitigation.
Source dated 2026 reports: Residents use rooftop storage, conservation, sharing and household adjustments, absorbing service-gap costs.
Source dated 2022 reports: Under SSP5-8.5, modeled drought frequency generally rises across Jordan by mid-term; the report identifies Amman and areas south of the city as future flood-risk locations.
Source dated 2024-02-11 reports: Conflict-driven Syrian refugee arrivals strained water systems in Irbid and Mafraq; remote infrastructure was aged.

ICRC's summary of an external before/after evaluation reports pumping-station operational efficiency rising from 20% to 86% after intervention, then falling to 65% by 2022 amid maintenance, parts and staffing constraints.
Source dated 2024-02-11 reports: Supply rose from 32 to 107 litres per capita daily, then 85 in 2022; people below 20 litres fell from 26,000 to 6,000.

ICRC described a Hofa workshop/training centre planned for completion at end-2023 and operator training for four northern governorates. The report does not verify later building completion or long-term maintenance outcomes.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification or human approval. 17 of 18 evidence records and 1 of 1 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
The IWMI 2024 Irbid–Ramtha vulnerability report was located, but its official item page returned HTTP 429 and the original report was not inspected; search metadata was not used as evidence.

The reviewed climate-security roadmap is a 2023 qualitative national synthesis; no current 2026 local study was found verifying its prospective climate–security pathways in specific Jordanian districts.
The UN-Habitat Mafraq survey is limited to 70 households in one neighborhood; its differences should not be generalized to all refugee-hosting communities.
No inspected primary passage established that water scarcity caused conflict; climate-security links are recorded only as conditional pathways explicitly stated by Adelphi.
The Mafraq survey's 70 households cannot support national claims or measured climate causation. Aquifer over-abstraction and formal service-access barriers are not reduced to climate alone.
The national qualitative climate-security roadmap supplies a conditional mechanism, not observed local water-caused violence. Refugee status is not treated as a propensity for violence.
ICRC documents both post-intervention gains and subsequent maintenance-related deterioration. The Hofa building's planned completion is not verified here.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
